writing.rule: Use the same validated ID across a request and its child operations.
writing.explanation:
Async work interleaves. Two requests can emit similar messages on one thread, so thread identity alone does not connect the messages that belong together. Give an operation one request ID, propagate it through database calls and retries, and record child work under the same parent context.

An incoming ID is untrusted data. Accept only a bounded ASCII token here, using letters, digits, dash and underscore; otherwise use a generated fallback supplied by the caller. Reject line breaks so an identifier cannot inject a fake log record. Do not treat a correlation ID as authentication or an idempotency key. Clients can choose or repeat it, and tracing systems have their own full trace-context format. This exercise isolates a small application request-ID policy rather than pretending to implement W3C traceparent.

The route project is Task Ledger: first keep a reproducible source history, then expose its data through a CLI and HTTP boundary, persist it in SQL, diagnose failures and prepare a release. This lesson owns one contract in that project. Run the worked example before changing the starter and explain which input makes the tempting shortcut fail.

Terminal practice: Send curl -i -H "X-Request-ID: req_42" http://127.0.0.1:8080/health and follow the same ID through the diagnostic output.

The compiler lab is independent of the reading question. Edit solution.rs; the app supplies a separate caller with normal, empty and adversarial inputs. A successful unchanged demonstration does not prove your implementation. After the lab, apply the same contract to the route companion project. Its README separates the on-device adapter from the desktop Cargo/TCP profile.
writing.exampleCaption: The worked implementation exercises validate a bounded correlation id. Its tests demonstrate the stated finite contract.
writing.task: Accept incoming IDs with 1..=64 bytes composed only of ASCII letters,digits,dash,underscore. Otherwise return the supplied fallback, which the caller guarantees is valid. Keep the public signature. Open the compiler lab and edit solution.rs; do not edit the private verification caller.
writing.success: The separate caller accepts the changed solution and rejects unchanged TODO, a wrong implementation and a printed success message.
writing.question: Does a client-supplied request ID authenticate the caller?
answers: Yes, a unique-looking string proves identity
writing.feedback: Correlation identifies related events, not who is allowed to perform an operation.
